bull_bear.body: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; emphasized margin discipline, one-order-a-day discipline, and export revenue steadiness; no speculation on pipeline orders; clear commitment to consultancy DNA and debt-free model

bull_bear.body: Turnkey orders are consultancy in scope (5-6% fee) but booked as turnkey revenue — this inflates top line but doesn't change economics; export revenue is now quarterly and not episodic; QA revenue from non-IR clients is now >65%, reducing dependency on Indian Railways
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "93.7% Dividend Payout" is flagged as a headline of the quarter, with the Board declaring an "Interim Dividend of Rs 1.4 per share".
- The deck presents no capex plan, borrowing profile, balance-sheet or cash-flow disclosure, so payout is the only capital-allocation lever it discloses.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- licence/regulatory: designated nodal agency and export arm of the Ministry of Railways for rolling stock built by Indian Railways production units and domestic OEMs — evidence: supplied all 10 cape-gauge locomotives to CFM Mozambique and is supplying 200 passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway (EIB-funded global tender) — against it: the export business revived only 'after a gap of several years', and export orders are won 'through global competitive tenders'
- licence/regulatory: authorised inspection & testing agency for Indian Railways — evidence: 'Authorized inspection & testing agency of Rails at SAIL Bhilai & JSPL Raigad for Indian Railways'; attended more than 1,00,000 inspection calls during the year
- licence/regulatory: REMC Limited (51% RITES, 49% Indian Railways) holds the mandate for Indian Railways' open-access power procurement — evidence: 'REMC Limited, which has a mandate to handle the power procurement under 'open access' for Indian Railways'
- licence/regulatory: empanelled transaction advisor to government for PPP and NHAI asset monetisation — evidence: empanelled with the Department of Economic Affairs for PPP projects and with NHAI for InvIT and TOT monetisation; advised on NHAI's first public InvIT (Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust) — against it: the report flags 'the shift toward competitive bidding' and 'growing private sector involvement' as pressures on margins and revenue visibility
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Intensifying competition and competitive procurement models — Competition from domestic and global engineering consultants, wider adoption of competitive procurement models, increasing project complexity and evolving sustainability and digital requirements may exert pressure on margins and execution capabilities.
- Dependence on public capital expenditure and project approvals — The company is exposed to fluctuations in public capital expenditure, delays in project approvals and project implementation timelines.
- International business exposure: geopolitics, regulation and foreign exchange — Geopolitical uncertainties, regulatory changes and foreign exchange fluctuations may impact performance, particularly in international markets; forex is called a key financial risk given the growing international project portfolio, managed via a Currency Risk Management Policy and Treasury Risk Management Committee.
- Availability and retention of skilled professionals — Competition for specialised engineering and project-management talent has intensified across the infrastructure sector; availability and retention of skilled professionals is described as an important area of focus.
- Rapid technological change and rising capability requirements — Growing client demand for digital engineering, sustainable infrastructure, integrated mobility and advanced project management requires continuous capability enhancement and investment; increasing project complexity may strain execution capabilities.
- Supply chain disruptions — Supply chain disruptions are named among factors that may impact business performance, particularly in international markets.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Consultancy: 12% YoY growth, 30%+ margins; Export: INR 60cr revenue in Q2 (first after 2-year gap), 10% margin, 10 locos to Mozambique (2 delivered, 2 shipped in Oct), 160cr order for SA locos; Turnkey: -INR 90cr YoY due to execution lag, 1-2% margins; Leasing: >100 locomotives leased, 30%+ margins, growing steadily

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Headline self-description is a "One order a Day company", with the added claim that it "continued to securing one exports order every quarter".
- Order book as on 30.06.2026 is called the "Highest Ever Order book at Rs 9445 crore", with "Rs 670+ crore of new orders (Incl. extension)" added during the quarter.
- Order book is split "Nomination vs Competition" at Nomination 38% and Competition 62%, indicating a mix of government-nominated and competitively won work.
- Signed an MoU "with CRISIL for integrated, data-driven infrastructure solutions".
- Client roster in the quarter spans central/state and PSU bodies — Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, NALCO, Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power, Mormugao Port Authority, Steel Authority of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, Northern Railways — plus an overseas client, Medha Mobility Australia Pty. Limited.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Major contracts secured Q1FY27] Largest disclosed wins are Project Management Consultancy for Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Lucknow at Rs 169 Cr (completion 2028); NALCO PMC extension for the Sankerjang railway siding, Orissa at Rs 39 Cr (2026); Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power locomotive wet-lease and siding O&M at Rs 29 Cr (2030); Mormugao Port Authority locomotive hire at Rs 21 Cr (2031); SAIL WDS6 locomotive overhauling at Bokaro at Rs 20 Cr (2028); Ministry of Home Affairs third-party inspection of ICBR-II roads at Rs 16 Cr (2029); Medha Mobility Australia locomotive supply at Rs 9 Cr (2026); and a Northern Railways Delhi station decongestion study at Rs 8 Cr (2027).
- [Employee productivity] Revenue per employee is shown as 0.99, 1.06, 0.97, 0.87 and 0.90 (Rs Cr) for FY22-FY26 and 0.18 for both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27; PAT per employee is 0.19, 0.21, 0.18, 0.15, 0.15 for FY22-FY26 and 0.025 for both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 — standalone, based on the average quarterly employee count.
- [Restatement] "Due to reclassification of reversal of provisions from other operating income to expenses, revenue have been restated in Q1FY26", applied to both total and segmental revenue, so year-on-year comparisons in the deck are against a restated base.
- [Unallocable expenses] Segmental profit table carries un-allocable expenses of Rs 36 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 32 crore in Q1FY26, i.e. segment profits shown do not net down to reported profit.
- [Internal contradiction] The round-up slide says the quarter added "Rs 670+ crore of new orders (Incl. extension)" while the order book slide states "Rs 674 Crore" and "including extensions of Rs 674 crore"; both readings are as printed.
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: RITES provides engineering consultancy across the project lifecycle (feasibility studies, DPRs, design engineering, project management, construction supervision, transaction advisory and third-party inspection/quality assurance) for railways, metros, highways, bridges, ports, airports and urban infrastructure. It also leases and maintains locomotives and wagons for non-railway clients in power, steel, port and logistics sectors, and acts as the nodal agency for export of rolling stock made by Indian Railways production units and domestic OEMs. Clients are government agencies, public sector enterprises, multilateral institutions and international clients.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Consultancy - rail infrastructure & highways:** Feasibility studies and DPRs, Detailed engineering and design, Project management consultancy (PMC), Construction supervision, Structural health monitoring
- **Consultancy - urban engineering & green mobility:** Metro/MRTS feasibility studies, AARs and DPRs, Comprehensive Mobility Plans, Traffic engineering and transport demand modelling, Transit-oriented development studies, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Green Mobility Action Plans
- **Consultancy - transport economics:** Transport master plans, Logistics master plans and multimodal logistics parks, Rail connectivity studies, Economic and financial appraisal
- **Transaction advisory:** PPP transaction advisory, Asset monetisation advisory (InvIT / TOT), Project appraisal and structuring, Bid process management
- **Quality assurance:** Third-party inspection in India and abroad, Independent Safety Assessment, Product conformity assessment, Material testing (SHODH laboratories), AI-based inspection (VISTAR)
- **Leasing & O&M:** Wet leasing of locomotives, Operation and maintenance of locomotives and wagons, Train running in private yards and sidings, Periodic overhaul of locomotives, wagons and DG sets
- **Export:** Electric and diesel locomotives, DEMU trainsets, Semi high-speed trainsets (Vande Bharat), Passenger coaches, Rolling-stock spares and after-sales support, Rolling-stock maintenance facility consultancy/turnkey

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- 3Ds strategic lens: Diversification (new markets, clients and sectors), Digitalisation (AI, digital monitoring, data) and Decarbonisation (green, low-carbon infrastructure solutions).
- RITES Videsh: Regional Business Heads appointed for five strategic geographies, with operational offices in Manila, Abu Dhabi and Georgetown and new offices in Johannesburg and Accra being established.
- Strategic shift toward collaborative and higher-margin consultancy opportunities, with sharpened focus on high-value project consultancy, export revival, strategic partnerships and technology-enabled delivery.
- Strategic MoUs and partnerships with the Government of Botswana, CONCOR, SAIL and DP World covering railway modernisation, logistics infrastructure, locomotive leasing and data-driven advisory.
- Move from an expertise-led to a market-led, technology-enabled and outcome-focused model; shift from execution-centric delivery to tech-driven solutions.
- Technology build-out: Centre of Excellence 'Abhikalp', AI-enabled inspection solution 'VISTAR', project-planning tool 'PARAKH', Industry 4.0 for operational efficiency.
- Diversify the client base across government, public-sector and private-sector clients and develop specialised, high-value services.
- Workforce readiness for AI-driven infrastructure through the #aiReady initiative and the 'Lakshya' leadership series.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: RITES is an asset-light consultancy; the report discloses no manufacturing capacity additions. Expansion is geographic and capability-led: under the RITES Videsh initiative it has initiated five Regional Business Offices (Ghana for Central and West Africa, UAE for Middle East and North Africa, South Africa for South and East Africa, the Philippines for Southeast Asia, Guyana for South America), with offices in Manila, Abu Dhabi and Georgetown operational and Johannesburg and Accra being established. Export execution includes the 200-coach Bangladesh Railway contract, with the first 20-coach rake slated for the forthcoming financial year.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Export business revived after a gap of several years; export orders secured through global competitive tenders are now starting to contribute to revenue.
- The young order book has already begun generating revenue.
- Turnkey revenue dipped as older orders were completed while newer ones were only beginning to contribute to revenue.
- Management acknowledges margin pressures; the shift to collaborative, higher-margin consultancy helped offset external pressures.
- Company sees itself positioned to benefit from technical consultancy, asset-light project execution and export of indigenously developed rolling stock amid emphasis on integrated, resilient and sustainable transport networks.
- Consultancy remains the principal revenue driver and cornerstone of the business; leasing reached its highest-ever revenue.
- All-time high order book of Rs 9,416 crore as on March 31, 2026, described as providing strong visibility for future revenues.
- Maintained a strike rate of securing one order a day across consultancy, turnkey, leasing and export businesses.
- Secured a Rs 915 crore contract to supply 200 broad-gauge passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Navratna public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Railways offering multidisciplinary transport-infrastructure consultancy, quality assurance, locomotive leasing and rolling-stock exports.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: RITES provides engineering consultancy across the project lifecycle (feasibility studies, DPRs, design engineering, project management, construction supervision, transaction advisory and third-party inspection/quality assurance) for railways, metros, highways, bridges, ports, airports and urban infrastructure. It also leases and maintains locomotives and wagons for non-railway clients in power, steel, port and logistics sectors, and acts as the nodal agency for export of rolling stock made by Indian Railways production units and domestic OEMs. Clients are government agencies, public sector enterprises, multilateral institutions and international clients.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- RITES (Afrika) (Pty) Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned (100%) foreign subsidiary based in Botswana; maintains presence through project execution in the region.
- REMC Limited — subsidiary: 51% held by RITES; Indian Railway holds the other 49%.
- SAIL-RITES Bengal Wagon Industry Private Limited — JV: Joint venture of RITES and SAIL; RITES holds 50%.
- Indian Railway Stations Development Corporation Limited — JV: Joint venture of RITES, RLDA and IRCON; RITES holds 24%.
- Elicius Energy Private Limited — associate: Associate; RITES holds 13%.
- Metro Management Group Limited — associate: Associate; RITES holds 24.5%.

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Consultancy: 12% YoY growth, 30%+ margins; Export: INR 60cr revenue in Q2 (first after 2-year gap), 10% margin, 10 locos to Mozambique (2 delivered, 2 shipped in Oct), 160cr order for SA locos; Turnkey: -INR 90cr YoY due to execution lag, 1-2% margins; Leasing: >100 locomotives leased, 30%+ margins, growing steadily

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Consultancy - rail infrastructure & highways:** Feasibility studies and DPRs, Detailed engineering and design, Project management consultancy (PMC), Construction supervision, Structural health monitoring
- **Consultancy - urban engineering & green mobility:** Metro/MRTS feasibility studies, AARs and DPRs, Comprehensive Mobility Plans, Traffic engineering and transport demand modelling, Transit-oriented development studies, Environmental and Social Impact Assessment, Green Mobility Action Plans
- **Consultancy - transport economics:** Transport master plans, Logistics master plans and multimodal logistics parks, Rail connectivity studies, Economic and financial appraisal
- **Transaction advisory:** PPP transaction advisory, Asset monetisation advisory (InvIT / TOT), Project appraisal and structuring, Bid process management
- **Quality assurance:** Third-party inspection in India and abroad, Independent Safety Assessment, Product conformity assessment, Material testing (SHODH laboratories), AI-based inspection (VISTAR)
- **Leasing & O&M:** Wet leasing of locomotives, Operation and maintenance of locomotives and wagons, Train running in private yards and sidings, Periodic overhaul of locomotives, wagons and DG sets
- **Export:** Electric and diesel locomotives, DEMU trainsets, Semi high-speed trainsets (Vande Bharat), Passenger coaches, Rolling-stock spares and after-sales support, Rolling-stock maintenance facility consultancy/turnkey

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Indian Railways / Ministry of Railways
- Power sector (NTPC, State Electricity Boards)
- Steel (SAIL, TATA, JSPL)
- Ports (Visakhapatnam, Mormugaon, Dhamra, Gopalpur)
- Coal and mining companies
- Urban transport / metro authorities
- Highways (NHAI)
- Africa (Mozambique, Botswana)
- South Asia (Bangladesh, Sri Lanka)
- Middle East (UAE)
- South East Asia
- Latin America

certifications.title: Quality certifications
certifications.body:
- ISO 17020 accreditation (QA vertical, NABCB)
- ISO 17065 accreditation (QA vertical, NABCB)
- ISO/IEC 17025:2017 (NABL) for all four material testing laboratories

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: INR 9,090cr (all-time high): Turnkey INR 4,300cr; Consultancy INR 2,930cr; Export INR 1,540cr; Leasing/REMC INR 320cr

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: Revenue growth: targeting double-digit YoY by FY26 end; EBITDA margin: >20% baseline maintained; Order inflow: >1 order/day sustained; Capex: minimal (<1% of revenue); Commissioning: Mozambique locos (Q1FY27), Bangladesh coaches (Q1FY27)

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Middle East expansion via Etihad Rail MoU; Vande Bharat ISA certification JV with DNV; Non-IR quality assurance clients now >65% of QA revenue; Potential in metro, highway, and airport PMC projects

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Export business revived after a gap of several years; export orders secured through global competitive tenders are now starting to contribute to revenue.
- The young order book has already begun generating revenue.
- Turnkey revenue dipped as older orders were completed while newer ones were only beginning to contribute to revenue.
- Management acknowledges margin pressures; the shift to collaborative, higher-margin consultancy helped offset external pressures.
- Company sees itself positioned to benefit from technical consultancy, asset-light project execution and export of indigenously developed rolling stock amid emphasis on integrated, resilient and sustainable transport networks.
- Consultancy remains the principal revenue driver and cornerstone of the business; leasing reached its highest-ever revenue.
- All-time high order book of Rs 9,416 crore as on March 31, 2026, described as providing strong visibility for future revenues.
- Maintained a strike rate of securing one order a day across consultancy, turnkey, leasing and export businesses.
- Secured a Rs 915 crore contract to supply 200 broad-gauge passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Consultancy: 30%+ (stable); Export: ~10% (initial, expected to stabilize); Turnkey: 1-2%; Leasing: 30%+; Cost pressure managed via diversification and premium consultancy mix; No material input cost inflation cited

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: 100% internal accruals; zero debt; 94% dividend payout ratio maintained; no M&A or buybacks announced; focus on organic growth and margin preservation

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: RITES is an asset-light consultancy; the report discloses no manufacturing capacity additions. Expansion is geographic and capability-led: under the RITES Videsh initiative it has initiated five Regional Business Offices (Ghana for Central and West Africa, UAE for Middle East and North Africa, South Africa for South and East Africa, the Philippines for Southeast Asia, Guyana for South America), with offices in Manila, Abu Dhabi and Georgetown operational and Johannesburg and Accra being established. Export execution includes the 200-coach Bangladesh Railway contract, with the first 20-coach rake slated for the forthcoming financial year.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, disciplined, and execution-focused; emphasized margin discipline, one-order-a-day discipline, and export revenue steadiness; no speculation on pipeline orders; clear commitment to consultancy DNA and debt-free model

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- licence/regulatory: designated nodal agency and export arm of the Ministry of Railways for rolling stock built by Indian Railways production units and domestic OEMs — evidence: supplied all 10 cape-gauge locomotives to CFM Mozambique and is supplying 200 passenger coaches to Bangladesh Railway (EIB-funded global tender) — against it: the export business revived only 'after a gap of several years', and export orders are won 'through global competitive tenders'
- licence/regulatory: authorised inspection & testing agency for Indian Railways — evidence: 'Authorized inspection & testing agency of Rails at SAIL Bhilai & JSPL Raigad for Indian Railways'; attended more than 1,00,000 inspection calls during the year
- licence/regulatory: REMC Limited (51% RITES, 49% Indian Railways) holds the mandate for Indian Railways' open-access power procurement — evidence: 'REMC Limited, which has a mandate to handle the power procurement under 'open access' for Indian Railways'
- licence/regulatory: empanelled transaction advisor to government for PPP and NHAI asset monetisation — evidence: empanelled with the Department of Economic Affairs for PPP projects and with NHAI for InvIT and TOT monetisation; advised on NHAI's first public InvIT (Raajmarg Infra Investment Trust) — against it: the report flags 'the shift toward competitive bidding' and 'growing private sector involvement' as pressures on margins and revenue visibility

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Turnkey revenue delay beyond Q1FY27; export revenue seasonality if order pipeline falters; competitive margin erosion in consultancy; geopolitical delays in Africa/Middle East projects; superannuation churn (300 inducted, 200+ retired in H1)

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Turnkey orders are consultancy in scope (5-6% fee) but booked as turnkey revenue — this inflates top line but doesn't change economics; export revenue is now quarterly and not episodic; QA revenue from non-IR clients is now >65%, reducing dependency on Indian Railways

strategy.body:
- 3Ds strategic lens: Diversification (new markets, clients and sectors), Digitalisation (AI, digital monitoring, data) and Decarbonisation (green, low-carbon infrastructure solutions).
- RITES Videsh: Regional Business Heads appointed for five strategic geographies, with operational offices in Manila, Abu Dhabi and Georgetown and new offices in Johannesburg and Accra being established.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Major contracts secured Q1FY27] Largest disclosed wins are Project Management Consultancy for Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar University, Lucknow at Rs 169 Cr (completion 2028); NALCO PMC extension for the Sankerjang railway siding, Orissa at Rs 39 Cr (2026); Neyveli Uttar Pradesh Power locomotive wet-lease and siding O&M at Rs 29 Cr (2030); Mormugao Port Authority locomotive hire at Rs 21 Cr (2031); SAIL WDS6 locomotive overhauling at Bokaro at Rs 20 Cr (2028); Ministry of Home Affairs third-party inspection of ICBR-II roads at Rs 16 Cr (2029); Medha Mobility Australia locomotive supply at Rs 9 Cr (2026); and a Northern Railways Delhi station decongestion study at Rs 8 Cr (2027).
- [Employee productivity] Revenue per employee is shown as 0.99, 1.06, 0.97, 0.87 and 0.90 (Rs Cr) for FY22-FY26 and 0.18 for both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27; PAT per employee is 0.19, 0.21, 0.18, 0.15, 0.15 for FY22-FY26 and 0.025 for both Q1FY26 and Q1FY27 — standalone, based on the average quarterly employee count.
- [Restatement] "Due to reclassification of reversal of provisions from other operating income to expenses, revenue have been restated in Q1FY26", applied to both total and segmental revenue, so year-on-year comparisons in the deck are against a restated base.
- [Unallocable expenses] Segmental profit table carries un-allocable expenses of Rs 36 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 32 crore in Q1FY26, i.e. segment profits shown do not net down to reported profit.
- [Internal contradiction] The round-up slide says the quarter added "Rs 670+ crore of new orders (Incl. extension)" while the order book slide states "Rs 674 Crore" and "including extensions of Rs 674 crore"; both readings are as printed.

themes.title: Railway rolling-stock & component capex
themes.need: A ~INR2.65 lakh cr Railways capital outlay and a pending ~1-lakh-wagon tender ('anytime this year' per JWL) drive rolling-stock, wheelsets, springs, castings, bogie components and interiors - with deep import-substitution (Neetu Yoshi 544434 castings; Airfloa 544516 interiors; Concord 543619 electronics). TITAGARH/TEXRAIL/JWL lead wagons; RVNL/IRCON/GPTINFRA on rail EPC.
themes.driver: Indian Railways large wagon tender award (next 1-2 quarters); wheelset plant ramp; Vande Bharat / Kavach orders.

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
